work: Register the exact X500 V2 source documents and reference revisions; distinguish old build examples from the chosen geometry.
expected_evidence: Source register with URL, revision/date where available, access status and the specific fact supported. No mixed revisions hidden in the BOM.

work: Define the station boundary, incoming product state and downstream assembly needs. Resolve whether the lower plate arrives with PDB/wiring or other inaccessible items fitted.
expected_evidence: One-page input/output contract; every operation belongs to upstream work, this cell or downstream work.

work: Produce the station BOM and operation-level consumption list, including fastener quantities and supplier arm modules.
expected_evidence: BOM with quantities, identities and status; one frame's required materials reconcile with its operations.

work: Write the manual reference assembly route and precedence constraints using the existing guide; note access and wire-management requirements.
expected_evidence: Ordered operation list and annotated assembly images; no robot assumptions yet.
note: Source/CAD annotated views are explicitly deferred to S1; no verified geometry claimed.

work: Define accepted, held, reworked and scrapped product conditions, plus inspection coverage.
expected_evidence: Product-quality requirements mapped to observable checks; unsupported physical performance is excluded from the pass claim.

work: Register engineering inputs: dimensions, mass, centre of gravity, thread/drive geometry, tightening recipe, operation times and replenishment. Mark each sourced, measured, CAD-derived or assumed.
expected_evidence: Parameter register with units, provenance, range/status and impact. Unknowns cannot masquerade as manufacturer data.

work: Convert requirements to verification cases and prioritize feasibility risks.
expected_evidence: Requirements-to-test matrix and risk register; every project claim has a proposed evidence path.

work: Obtain and inspect existing CAD first. Check scale, units, revision, component separation, missing items and permitted reuse. Create simplified geometry only for a documented gap.
expected_evidence: CAD inventory and reference-dimension checks; every proxy is labeled and excluded from unsupported clearance claims.
note: Nominal CAD baseline. Current supplier geometry and arm identity mapping remain open.

work: Define part datums, arm identities, assembly poses and a joint table for all frame screws/nuts. Establish the insertion side, head access and nut envelope.
expected_evidence: Labeled product drawing and joint map; each fastener has one physical location and its actual mating parts.
note: Sixteen central screw/nut center positions extracted. Still verify supplier-arm mapping, mating geometry and fastening access.

work: Perform the assembly/access study: ordering, wire parking, part insertion, top-plate closure, downstream access and extraction.
expected_evidence: Section views and a feasible sequence; access conflicts resolved before motion design.

work: Design the fixture: location, support, anti-rotation nut pockets, nut loading/checking, clamps and release. Address loose nuts and cable traps explicitly.
expected_evidence: Fixture concept with loading/clamping/unloading states and clearance evidence; neither floating nuts nor blocked extraction.

work: Compare existing screwdriving/feeding options against the exact joint. Start with indexed screw presentation; verify length, head, bit, retention, axial travel and nose clearance. Define provisional joint-control stages.
expected_evidence: Tool compatibility matrix and fastening concept; screw-size advertising is not used as complete proof. No unsourced final torque.

work: Select a candidate robot/tool arrangement from documented models. Verify payload including tooling, centre of gravity/inertia, grasp surfaces, reach, orientation and tool-change needs. Lay out operator/service access.
expected_evidence: Candidate layout, robot/tool specification references, grasp list and reach/access evidence; choice remains rejectable if geometry fails.

work: Review the complete mechanical concept against product requirements and failure/recovery needs.
expected_evidence: Design-review checklist with resolved blockers. If automation is infeasible, document the smallest justified boundary/tool change instead of hiding it.

work: Create the approved repository and milestone/issue structure. Configure one-active-task workflow, reproducible local commands, automated checks and a minimal Vercel preview.
expected_evidence: A clean checkout can run/build the minimal app; repository and deployment visibility follow the approved scope.

work: Define typed schemas for product, station, operation, joint, tool, sensor, material, run and result. Centralize units and coordinate conventions.
expected_evidence: Versioned schemas and sample configuration; invalid/missing values are rejected with useful errors.

work: Implement the deterministic simulation clock, event queue and station state machine independently of rendering.
expected_evidence: The same input and seed produces the same ordered results; pause/step/accelerate do not change process outcomes.

work: Implement device commands, permission checks, completion feedback and timeouts. Track robot, fixture, tools and operator as resources.
expected_evidence: State-transition tests show no action completing solely because its command was sent.

work: Implement product/part ownership and event records. A part belongs to exactly one tray, gripper, fixture or output location.
expected_evidence: Material and ownership invariants hold; event export identifies the active assembly and recipe.

work: Add essential verification: no negative inventory, duplicate joint acceptance, overlapping single-robot tasks or successful unload without a supported product.
expected_evidence: Focused engine tests pass; invalid sequences are rejected and logged.

work: Provide a plain engineering interface for mode, start, stop, reset, step and state/event inspection.
expected_evidence: A reviewer can execute a simple cycle and understand why a command is permitted or blocked.

work: Import approved geometry and establish world, robot-base, tool, fixture, tray and part coordinate frames. Keep source CAD separate from optimized display meshes.
expected_evidence: Scaled scene plus transform checks; rendering simplification does not change engineering datum positions.

work: Implement explicit operator loading and unloading permissions, durations and completion events.
expected_evidence: Operator actions consume time/resources; loading while automatic access is prohibited cannot succeed.

work: Implement fixture seating, clamps and retained-nut state with separate command/feedback.
expected_evidence: Missing/misseated parts or absent clamp confirmation prevent fastening. Fixture release preserves support requirements.

work: Implement known-position trays, nut/screw presentation, inventory and replenishment.
expected_evidence: Every consumption/replenishment reconciles with stock; empty positions produce waiting or a defined fault.

work: Implement the screwdriver's device interface and approach/engagement concept without assuming a valid joint result.
expected_evidence: Device states and provisional recipes are visible; result signals remain separate from the rendered tool movement.

work: Implement accepted output, held-product location and capacity-limited unload.
expected_evidence: A full output location blocks release/transfer appropriately; a held product cannot enter accepted stock.

work: Demonstrate the operator-loaded baseline and review its work sequence and event history.
expected_evidence: One reference frame flows through the modeled work; manual and automatic work are clearly separated.

work: Encode the approved joint list, fastening sequence and recipe revision. Associate every joint with its required screw/nut and fixture support.
expected_evidence: Joint table matches the assembly; missing/duplicated positions cannot satisfy completion.

work: Implement screwdriver acquisition/docking and tool-lock/identity checks, with the physical access envelope established in S1.
expected_evidence: Robot cannot drive with the wrong/unlocked tool; docking and tool changes consume explicit time.

work: Implement screw acquisition from indexed presentation and travel to the joint. Resolve long-screw retention/clearance and motor-wire proximity.
expected_evidence: Screw ownership is preserved; absent screw, failed pick or obstructed path is handled explicitly.

work: Model engagement, rundown and final tightening as distinct operations. Represent nut locking resistance and suspicious early torque/insufficient engagement as testable cases.
expected_evidence: Joint-result model distinguishes success from commanded torque. Synthetic signatures are labeled, not presented as measured tool curves.

work: Record each attempt's joint ID, recipe, reported torque/angle/depth where supported, status and failure reason. Separate instrument availability from desired data.
expected_evidence: One joint's result cannot be applied to another assembly, location or recipe. Unsupported sensing is not fabricated.

work: Verify faults: missing nut, wrong screw, cross-thread-like engagement, spinning nut, tool timeout and incomplete sequence. Define their observable signatures/coverage.
expected_evidence: Detected faults hold the cycle; undetectable conditions are recorded as coverage gaps rather than magically found.

work: Demonstrate complete fastening and compare modeled time with its operation breakdown and source status.
expected_evidence: Every required joint has the proper accepted record; total process time equals accounted actions and waits.

work: Implement the selected robot's joint model, limits, tool transforms, payload metadata and motion constraints. Use existing documented models first.
expected_evidence: Joint-limited poses and paths are reproducible; a Cartesian animation without a valid robot configuration is not marked verified.

work: Implement the approved grasp and release model for lower plate, each arm, upper plate and completed assembly. Account for fingers, cables, motors and product support.
expected_evidence: Each grasp has an approach, grip confirmation, transport, seating and release condition; held parts move with the tool.

work: Implement lower-plate and four-arm placement with identity checks and wire parking. Preserve the actual insertion order from the mechanical study.
expected_evidence: Wrong arm/orientation and failed seating prevent subsequent closure; no hidden teleporting or preassembled replacement mesh.

work: Implement top-plate placement, fixture clamping and handoff to fastening. Tool changes must fit the actual single-robot sequence.
expected_evidence: Fixture holds the assembly independently before the robot releases it or changes tools; clamps leave every fastening path accessible.

work: Verify joint paths and collision clearance throughout approach, insertion, travel and tool changes, including held product, tool and cables' defined envelopes.
expected_evidence: Path review covers the moving envelope, not just endpoints; uncertain flexible-cable/contact behavior remains labeled.

work: Implement supported extraction and unload after accepted inspection. Verify nut-pocket release and grip access on the assembled product.
expected_evidence: No fixture trapping, part loss or unload into occupied space; output transfer is recorded once.

work: Demonstrate the integrated normal automatic cycle and identify remaining manual tasks.
expected_evidence: One assembly traverses all operations with consistent material, ownership, timing, joint and result records.

work: Implement mode/access permissions, stop, emergency-stop representation, acknowledgement and deliberate restart behavior. Define retained state for each interruption point.
expected_evidence: Closing access or acknowledging an alarm cannot silently resume motion. Product and joint history survive interruption.

work: Implement the fault catalogue below with explicit causes, observations, detection coverage, stop response and recovery prerequisites.
expected_evidence: Every fault has a reproducible scenario and an observable explanation; random failure alone is not a recovery design.

work: Implement held/rework/scrap disposition, failed-joint attempt history and controlled return to the proper sequence point.
expected_evidence: No unconditional retighten-until-pass behavior; intervention/replacement policy is recorded and counted.

work: Implement the inspection/control plan: incoming identity, seating, clamp state, fastening record completeness and final defined-feature inspection.
expected_evidence: Each quality requirement is linked to a detector or manual check and its coverage limit. False accept/reject scenarios can be represented.

work: Implement operator servicing: tray refill, screw/nut refill, bit/tool checks, calibration-due condition and fault intervention.
expected_evidence: Service actions consume operator availability, travel/service time and material. A single operator cannot service two cells simultaneously.

work: Verify information integrity: duplicate start, delayed/stale tool result, duplicate completion, wrong recipe and run reset during partial assembly.
expected_evidence: The cell does not double-count parts or accept a product with mismatched/stale evidence.

work: Run the normal, fault and recovery demonstrations and review all dispositions and downtime attribution.
expected_evidence: Failure cases either recover through their approved route or remain held; time and material are conserved.

work: Define available shift time, breaks, planned service, replenishment, arrivals, output removal and timing provenance. Separate operator work, robot work, tool work and waits.
expected_evidence: Transparent time budget and baseline operation-time breakdown; neither frame rate nor animation playback speed determines capacity.

work: Implement exact good/held/scrapped counts, first-pass yield, completed-cycle time, WIP, operator/robot utilization and categorized downtime.
expected_evidence: Metrics reconcile against event records and conservation equations; denominator definitions are visible.

work: Model repeated cycles, finite trays and shared operator service, including starvation, blocked output and changeovers where actually included.
expected_evidence: Capacity changes for explainable resource reasons; adding a robot does not automatically create free staffing or replenishment.

work: Define a bounded configuration catalogue: duplicate approved cell layouts, permitted operator counts and physical/service-space constraints. Keep product geometry fixed.
expected_evidence: Every candidate references the approved cell; invalid layouts or insufficient resources are rejected before evaluation.

work: Accept required good frames per shift and evaluate candidates. Use minimum cell count, then minimum operator count as the initial explicit ranking; use cost only if defensible cost inputs are supplied.
expected_evidence: Results show candidates, shortfalls and limiting reasons. No unsupported claim of a globally optimal factory or minimum actual cost.

work: Compare nominal and uncertain runs using a small fixed seed bank, the same seed set across candidates and a recorded compute cap. Expand runs only if needed to resolve an important difference.
expected_evidence: Export sample size, distribution assumptions, sample outputs and ranking stability. A sample success rate is not labeled a guarantee or statistical confidence without the relevant analysis.

work: Demonstrate a low-demand and higher-demand configuration plus an infeasible request. Explain how resources, waiting and good output change.
expected_evidence: Input changes cause a documented configuration decision; impossible requests produce a shortfall and limiting constraints rather than a fabricated solution.

work: Execute the virtual factory acceptance matrix below against pinned product, recipe, code and scenario versions. Resolve failed checks in order.
expected_evidence: Test evidence with expected/observed outcomes and explicit unresolved limitations.

work: Verify the model by independent hand checks: material balance, joint counts, deterministic cycle time, waiting cases and simple bottleneck bounds. Compare with physical or documented observations when obtainable.
expected_evidence: Explainable calculations and comparisons. Distinguish model verification from validation against a physical station.

work: Complete an appropriately scoped sensitivity study for the main uncertain inputs: handling time, fastening/service time, refill frequency, faults and rework.
expected_evidence: Identify which uncertainties materially change capacity conclusions; avoid claiming precision unsupported by inputs.

work: Finish the engineering HMI: inspect state, follow an assembly, view joint results, inject approved faults, acknowledge/recover, compare demand cases and export runs.
expected_evidence: Clear normal/held/fault states and readable units; a walkthrough is possible without developer knowledge.

work: Check web usability, asset rights, reproducible builds, capped worker runs, import validation and target-browser performance.
expected_evidence: A clean build and representative browser run pass; exact browser/hardware and remaining performance limits are recorded.

work: Prepare the final Git/Vercel release, source/model manifest, engineering summary, short demonstration and portfolio case study. Keep visibility/promotion within the user's authorization.
expected_evidence: Release candidate ties deployed source to a commit and includes setup instructions and downloadable evidence.

work: Review the project against its original goals, show normal/fault/demand scenarios and record final known limitations and follow-on backlog.
expected_evidence: A reviewer can reproduce the evidence and understand which behaviors are modeled, assumed, geometrically checked or physically validated.
